paragraphs.sourceText: （请于正式开考后半小时内完成该部分，之后将进行听力考试） Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay commenting on the saying "Help others, and you will be helped when you are in need " You can cite examples to illustrate your views. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：这一部分，你有30分钟的时间写一篇文章，评论“帮助别人，当你需要帮助时，你会得到帮助”，你可以举出例子来说明你的观点。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Question 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many European countries have been making the shift to electric vehicles and Germany has just stated that they plan to ban the sale of vehicles using gasoline and diesel as fuel by 2030. The country is also planning to reduce its carbon footprint by 80-95% by 2050, ___26___ a shift to green energy in the country. Effectively, the ban will include the registration of new cars in the country as they will not allow any gasoline ___27___ vehicle to be registered after 2030.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多欧洲国家一直在转向电动汽车，德国刚刚表示计划到2030年禁止销售以汽油和柴油为燃料的汽车。该国还计划到2050年将碳足迹减少80-95%，从而引发该国向绿色能源的转变。实际上，该禁令将包括在该国注册新车，因为 2030 年之后将不允许任何汽油动力车辆注册。

paragraphs.sourceText: Part of the reason this ban is being discussed and ___28___ is because energy officials see that they will not reach their emissions goals by 2050 if they do not ___29___ a large portion of vehicle emissions. The country is still ___30___ that it will meet its emissions goals, like reducing emissions by 40% by 2020, but the ___31___ of electric cars in the country has not occurred as fast as expected.
paragraphs.translationZh: 讨论和实施这项禁令的部分原因是能源官员认为，如果不消除大部分车辆排放，到 2050 年就无法实现排放目标。该国仍然对实现排放目标抱有希望，比如到 2020 年将排放量减少 40%，但该国对电动汽车的接受程度并没有像预期的那么快。

paragraphs.sourceText: Other efforts to increase the use of electric vehicles include plans to build over 1 million hybrid and electric car battery charging stations across the country. By 2030, Germany plans on having over 6 million charging stations ___32___. According to the International Business Times, electric car sales are expected to increase as Volkswagen is still recovering from its emissions scandal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 其他增加电动汽车使用的努力包括计划在全国建设超过 100 万个混合动力和电动汽车电池充电站。到 2030 年，德国计划安装超过 600 万个充电站。据《国际商业时报》报道，由于大众汽车仍在从排放丑闻中恢复过来，电动汽车销量预计将增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are ___33___ around 155,000 registered hybrid and electric vehicles on German roads, dwarfed by the 45 million gasoline and diesel cars driving there now. As countries continue setting goals of reducing emissions, greater steps need to be taken to have a ___34___ effect on the surrounding environment. While the efforts are certainly not ___35___, the results of such bans will likely only start to be seen by generations down the line, bettering the world for the future.
paragraphs.translationZh: 目前德国道路上约有 155,000 辆注册的混合动力和电动汽车，与目前行驶的 4500 万辆汽油和柴油汽车相比相形见绌。随着各国不断制定减排目标，需要采取更大的措施才能对周围环境产生显着影响。虽然这些努力肯定不是徒劳的，但此类禁令的结果可能只会开始被几代人看到，从而使世界的未来变得更加美好。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Apple’s Stance Highlights a More Confrontational Teach Industry
paragraphs.translationZh: 苹果的立场凸显了更具对抗性的教学行业

paragraphs.sourceText: A. The battle between Apple and law enforcement officials over unlocking a terrorist’s smartphone is the culmination of a slow turning of the tables between the technology industry and the United States government.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：苹果公司与执法官员之间关于解锁恐怖分子智能手机的斗争是科技行业与美国政府之间缓慢扭转局面的最终结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. After revelations by the former National Security Agency contractor Edward J. Snowden in 2013 that the government both cozied up to (讨好) certain tech companies and hacked into others to gain access to private data on an enormous scale, tech giants began to recognize the United States government as a hostile actor. But if the confrontation has crystallized in this latest battle, it may already be heading toward a predictable conclusion: In the long run, the tech companies are destined to emerge victorious.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 2013 年，前国家安全局承包商爱德华·J·斯诺登 (Edward J. Snowden) 揭露政府既讨好某些科技公司，又入侵其他公司以大规模获取私人数据，此后，科技巨头开始将美国政府视为敌对行为体。但如果这场最新的战斗中的对抗已经具体化，那么它可能已经走向一个可预见的结论：从长远来看，科技公司注定会取得胜利。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. It may not seem that way at the moment. On the one side, you have the United States government’s mighty legal and security apparatus fighting for data of the most sympathetic sort: the secrets buried in a dead mass murderer’s phone. The action stems from a federal court order issued on Tuesday requiring Apple to help the Federal Bureau of Investigation (F.B.I) to unlock an iPhone used by one of the two attackers who killed 14 people in San Bernardino, California, in December.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 目前看来可能并非如此。一方面，美国政府强大的法律和安全机构正在争夺最值得同情的数据：埋藏在已故大屠杀凶手手机中的秘密。该行动源于联邦法院周二发布的一项命令，要求苹果公司帮助联邦调查局 (FBI) 解锁 12 月在加利福尼亚州圣贝纳迪诺杀害 14 人的两名袭击者之一所使用的 iPhone。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. In the other corner is the world’s most valuable company, whose chief executive, Timothy D. Cook, has said he will appeal the court’s order. Apple argues that it is fighting to preserve a principle that most of us who are addicted to our smartphones can defend: Weaken a single iPhone so that its contents can be viewed by the American government and you risk weakening all iPhones for any government intruder, anywhere.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 另一个角落是世界上最有价值的公司，其首席执行官蒂莫西·D·库克 (Timothy D. Cook) 表示，他将对法院的命令提出上诉。苹果公司辩称，它正在努力维护我们大多数沉迷于智能手机的人都可以捍卫的原则：弱化一部 iPhone，以便美国政府可以查看其内容，而你则冒着为任何地方的任何政府入侵者弱化所有 iPhone 的风险。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. There will probably be months of legal tussling, and it is not at all clear which side will prevail in court, nor in the battle for public opinion and legislative favor. Yet underlying all of this is a simple dynamic: Apple, Google, Facebook and other companies hold most of the cards in this confrontation. They have our data, and their businesses depend on the global public’s collective belief that they will do everything they can to protect that data.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 可能会持续数月的法律斗争，而且根本不清楚哪一方会在法庭上占上风，也不清楚在争取公众舆论和立法支持的斗争中哪一方会占上风。然而，这一切背后隐藏着一个简单的动态：苹果、谷歌、Facebook 和其他公司在这场对抗中掌握着大部分牌。他们拥有我们的数据，他们的业务取决于全球公众的集体信念，即他们将尽一切努力保护这些数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: F. Any crack in that front could be fatal for tech companies that must operate worldwide. If Apple is forced to open up an iPhone for an American law enforcement investigation, what is to prevent it from doing so for a request from the Chinese or the Iranians? If Apple is forced to write code that lets the F.B.I. get into the Phone 5c used by Syed Rizwan Farook, the male attacker in the San Bernardino attack, who would be responsible if some hacker got hold of that code and broke into its other devices?
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 对于必须在全球范围内运营的科技公司来说，这方面的任何裂缝都可能是致命的。如果苹果公司被迫开放 iPhone 供美国执法部门调查，那么如何阻止它应中国或伊朗人的要求这样做呢？如果苹果被迫编写代码让联邦调查局 (FBI)进入圣贝纳迪诺袭击中的男性攻击者赛义德·里兹万·法鲁克 (Syed Rizwan Farook) 使用的 Phone 5c，如果黑客掌握了该代码并侵入了其他设备，谁将负责？

paragraphs.sourceText: G. Apple’s stance on these issues emerged post-Snowden, when the company started putting in place a series of technologies that, by default, make use of encryption to limit access to people’s data. More than that, Apple - and, in different ways, other tech companies, including Google, Facebook, Twitter and Microsoft - have made their opposition to the government’s claims a point of corporate pride.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 苹果在这些问题上的立场是在斯诺登之后出现的，当时该公司开始采用一系列技术，默认情况下，利用加密来限制对人们数据的访问。更重要的是，苹果公司以及其他科技公司，包括谷歌、Facebook、Twitter 和微软，都以不同的方式将反对政府的主张作为企业的骄傲。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. Appl’s emerging global brand is privacy; it has staked its corporate reputation, not to mention the investment of considerable technical and financial resources, on limiting the sort of mass surveillance that was uncovered by Mr. Snowden. So now, for many cases involving governmental intrusions into data, once-lonely privacy advocates find themselves fighting alongside the most powerful company in the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. Appl 的新兴全球品牌是隐私；它以自己的企业声誉为赌注，更不用说投入大量技术和财政资源来限制斯诺登揭露的大规模监视活动。因此，现在，在许多涉及政府入侵数据的案件中，曾经孤独的隐私倡导者发现自己与世界上最强大的公司并肩作战。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. “A comparison point is in the 1990s battles over encryption,” said Kurt Opsahl, general counsel of the Electronic Frontier Foundation, a privacy watchdog group. “Then you had a few companies involved, but not one of the largest companies in the world coming out with a lengthy and impassioned post, like we saw yesterday from Tim Cook. Its profile has really been raised.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I. “一个比较点是 20 世纪 90 年代关于加密的斗争，”隐私监管组织电子前沿基金会总法律顾问库尔特·奥普萨尔 (Kurt Opsahl) 说。 “然后有几家公司参与其中，但没有世界上最大的公司之一发表冗长而热情的帖子，就像我们昨天从蒂姆·库克那里看到的那样。它的形象确实得到了提升。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J. Apple and other tech companies hold another ace: the technical means to keep making their devices more and more inaccessible. Note that Apple’s public opposition to the government’s request is itself a hindrance to mass government intrusion. And to get at the contents of a single iPhone, the government says it needs a court order and Apple’s help to write new code; in earlier versions of the iPhone, ones that were created before Apple found religion on (热衷于) privacy, the
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 苹果和其他科技公司还掌握着另一张王牌：不断让他们的设备变得越来越难以访问的技术手段。请注意，苹果公开反对政府的要求本身就是对政府大规模入侵的阻碍。政府表示，要获取一部 iPhone 的内容，需要法院命令和苹果公司的帮助来编写新代码；在 iPhone 的早期版本中，这些版本是在苹果公司信仰隐私之前创建的，

paragraphs.sourceText: case, measures that it could put into place in the future will almost certainly be able to further limit the government’s reach.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在这种情况下，未来可能采取的措施几乎肯定会进一步限制政府的影响力。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. That’s not to say that the outcome of the San Bernardino case is insignificant. As Apple and several security experts have argued, an order compelling Apple to write software that gives the F.B.I. access to the iPhone in question would establish an unsettling precedent. The order essentially asks Apple to hack its own devices, and once it is in place, the precedent could be used to justify law enforcement efforts to get around encryption technologies in other investigations far removed from national security threats.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 这并不是说圣贝纳迪诺案的结果无关紧要。正如苹果公司和几位安全专家所说，一项迫使苹果公司编写软件的命令，让联邦调查局能够访问相关 iPhone 将开创一个令人不安的先例。该命令实质上要求苹果公司破解自己的设备，一旦实施，该先例可以用来证明执法部门在远离国家安全威胁的其他调查中绕过加密技术的努力是合理的。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. Once armed with a method for gaining access to iPhones, the government could ask to use it proactively (先发制人 地), before a suspected terrorist attack - leaving Apple in a bind as to whether to comply or risk an attack and suffer a public-relations nightmare. “This is a brand-new salvo in the war against encryption,” Mr. Opsahl said. “We’ve had plenty of debates in Congress and the media over whether the government should have a backdoor, and this is an end run around that - here they come with an order to create that backdoor.”
paragraphs.translationZh: M.一旦掌握了获取 iPhone 的方法，政府就可以在涉嫌恐怖袭击之前要求主动使用它，这让苹果陷入困境：是否遵守规定，还是冒着遭受袭击的风险，并遭受公关噩梦。 “这是反加密战争中的全新齐射，”奥普萨尔先生说。 “我们在国会和媒体上就政府是否应该设立后门进行了很多辩论，而这是为了解决这个问题——他们带着创建后门的命令来了。”

paragraphs.sourceText: N. Yet it’s worth noting that even if Apple ultimately loses this case, it has plenty of technical means to close a backdoor over time. “If they’re anywhere near worth their salt as engineers, I bet they’re rethinking their threat model as we speak,” said Jonathan Zdziarski, a digital forensic expert who studies the iPhone and its vulnerabilities.
paragraphs.translationZh: N. 然而值得注意的是，即使苹果最终输掉了这场官司，随着时间的推移，它也有足够的技术手段来关闭后门。研究 iPhone 及其漏洞的数字取证专家乔纳森·兹齐亚斯基 (Jonathan Zdziarski) 表示：“如果他们称得上工程师，我敢打赌，就在我们说话的时候，他们正在重新考虑他们的威胁模型。”

paragraphs.sourceText: O. One relatively simple fix, Mr. Zdziarski said, would be for Apple to modify future versions of the iPhone to require a user to enter a passcode before the phone will accept the sort of modified operating system that the F.B.I. wants Apple to create. That way, Apple could not unilaterally introduce a code that weakens the iPhone — a user would have to consent to it.
paragraphs.translationZh: Zdziarski 先生说，一个相对简单的解决办法是，苹果公司修改 iPhone 的未来版本，要求用户输入密码，然后手机才会接受 FBI 修改过的操作系统。想要苹果创造。这样，苹果就不能单方面引入削弱 iPhone 的代码——用户必须同意它。

paragraphs.sourceText: P) “Nothing is 100 percent hacker-proof,” Mr. Zdziarski said, but he pointed out that the judge’s order in this case required Apple to provide “reasonable security assistance” to unlock Mr. Farook’s phone. If Apple alters the security model of future iPhones so that even its own engineers’ “reasonable assistance” will not be able to crack a given device when compelled by the government, a precedent set in this case might lose its lasting force. In other words, even if the F.B.I. wins this case, in the long run, it loses.
paragraphs.translationZh: P) “没有什么是 100% 防黑客的，”Zdziarski 先生说，但他指出，法官在本案中的命令要求苹果公司提供“合理的安全协助”来解锁 Farook 先生的手机。如果苹果改变未来 iPhone 的安全模式，使得即使是苹果自己的工程师的“合理协助”也无法在政府强制下破解特定设备，那么本案中的先例可能会失去持久力。换句话说，即使联邦调查局 (FBI)这场官司赢了，从长远来看，却是输了。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. It is a popular belief that tech companies are committed to protecting their customers’ private data.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 人们普遍认为科技公司致力于保护客户的私人数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. The US government believes that its access to people’s iPhones could be used to prevent terrorist attacks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 美国政府认为，其对人们 iPhone 的访问可用于防止恐怖袭击。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. A federal court asked Apple to help the FBI access data in a terrorist’s iPhone.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 一家联邦法院要求苹果公司帮助联邦调查局访问恐怖分子 iPhone 中的数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Privacy advocates now have Apple fighting alongside them against government access to personal data.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 隐私权倡导者现在让苹果公司与他们并肩反对政府获取个人数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Snowden revealed that the American government had tried hard to access private data in massive scale.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 斯诺登透露，美国政府曾努力试图大规模获取私人数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. The FBI might have been able to access private data in earlier iPhones without Apple’s help.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 如果没有苹果的帮助，联邦调查局可能能够访问早期 iPhone 中的私人数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. After the Snowden incident, Apple made clear its position to counter government intrusion into personal data by means of encryption.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 斯诺登事件后，苹果公司明确表示，将通过加密手段对抗政府对个人数据的入侵。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. According to one digital expert, no iPhone can be entirely free from hacking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 据一位数字专家称，没有一款 iPhone 能够完全免受黑客攻击。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Timothy Cook’s long web post has helped enhance Apple’s image.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 蒂莫西·库克（Timothy Cook）的长篇网络帖子有助于提升苹果公司的形象。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Apple’s CEO has decided to appeal the federal court’s order to unlock a user’s iPhone.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 苹果公司首席执行官决定对联邦法院解锁用户 iPhone 的命令提出上诉。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Question 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: At the base of a mountain in Tanzania’s Gregory Rift, Lake Natron burns bright red, surrounded by the remains of animals that were unfortunate enough to fall into the salty water. Bats, swallows and more are chemically preserved in the pose in which they perished, sealed in the deposits of sodium carbonate in the water. The lake’s landscape is bizarre and deadly- and made even more so by the fact that it’s the place where nearly 75percent of the world’s flamingos(火烈鸟) are born.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在坦桑尼亚格雷戈里裂谷的一座山脚下，纳特龙湖燃烧着鲜红色，周围都是不幸落入咸水中的动物遗骸。蝙蝠、燕子等动物以化学方式保存在它们死亡时的姿势，并密封在水中的碳酸钠沉积物中。这个湖的景观奇特而致命，更何况这里是世界上近 75% 的火烈鸟的出生地。

paragraphs.sourceText: The water is so corrosive that it can burn the skin and eyes of unadapted animals. Flamingos, however, are the only species that actually makes life in the midst of all that death. Once every three or four years, when conditions are right, the lake is covered with the pink birds as they stop flight to breed. Three –quarters of the world’s flamingos fly over from other salt lakes in the Rift Valley and nest on salt- crystal islands that appear when the water is at specific level- too high and the birds can’t build their nests, too low and predators can more briskly across the lake bed and attack. When the water hits the right level. The baby birds are kept safe form predators by a corrosive ditch.
paragraphs.translationZh: 水的腐蚀性很强，会灼伤不适应环境的动物的皮肤和眼睛。然而，火烈鸟是唯一真正在死亡中重生的物种。每三四年一次，当条件合适时，湖面上就会布满粉红色的鸟儿，因为它们会停止飞行去繁殖。世界上四分之三的火烈鸟从东非大​​裂谷的其他盐湖飞来，在水位达到特定水平时出现的盐晶岛上筑巢——水位太高，鸟类无法筑巢，太低，捕食者可以更快地穿过湖床进行攻击。当水达到合适的水平时。一条腐蚀性沟渠可以保护幼鸟免受捕食者的侵害。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Flamingos have evolved very leathery skin on their legs so they can tolerate the salt water,” says David Harper, a professor at the University of Leicester. “ Humans cannot, and would die if their legs were exposed for any length of time.” So far this year, water levels have been too high for the flamingos to nest.
paragraphs.translationZh: “火烈鸟的腿上进化出了非常坚韧的皮肤，因此它们可以忍受盐水，”莱斯特大学教授大卫·哈珀说。 “人类不能，而且如果双腿暴露一段时间就会死亡。”今年到目前为止，水位太高，火烈鸟无法筑巢。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some fish, too, have had limited success vacationing at the lake as less salty lagoons (泻湖) form on the outer edges from hot springs flowing into Lake Natron. Three species of tilapia (罗非鱼) thrive there part-time. “Fish have a refuge in the streams and can expand into the lagoons when the lake is low and the lagoons are separate,” Harper said. “All the lagoons join when the lake is high and fish must retreat to their stream refuges or die.” Otherwise, no fish are able to survive in the naturally toxic lake.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一些鱼类在湖中度假的成功也有限，因为流入纳特龙湖的温泉在其外缘形成了咸度较低的泻湖。三种罗非鱼在这里兼职繁衍生息。哈珀说：“鱼类在溪流中避难，当湖水低且泻湖分开时，它们可以扩展到泻湖中。” “当湖水水位很高时，所有泻湖都会汇合在一起，鱼儿必须退回溪流避难所，否则就会死亡。”否则，没有鱼能够在天然有毒的湖中生存。

paragraphs.sourceText: This unique ecosystem may soon be under pressure. The Tanzanian government has once again started mining the lake for soda ash, used for making chemicals, glass and detergents. Although the planned operation will be located more than 40 miles away, drawing the soda ash in through pipelines, conservationists worry it could still upset the natural water cycle and breeding grounds. For now, though, life prevails – even in a lake that kills almost everything it touches.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这个独特的生态系统可能很快就会面临压力。坦桑尼亚政府再次开始在湖中开采纯碱，用于制造化学品、玻璃和清洁剂。尽管计划中的作业地点将在 40 多英里外，通过管道吸入纯碱，但环保人士担心，这仍然可能扰乱自然水循环和繁殖地。但就目前而言，生命依然存在——即使是在一个几乎杀死了它所接触到的一切的湖中。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is the season for some frantic last-minute math across the country, employees of all stripe are counting backward in an attempt to figure out just how much paid time-off they have left it their reserves. More of them, though, will skip those calculations altogether and just power through the holidays into 2017: More than half of American workers don’t use up all of their allotted vacation days each year.
paragraphs.translationZh: 全国各地都在进行最后一刻的疯狂数学计算，各行各业的员工都在倒数，试图算出他们还保留了多少带薪休假。不过，更多人会完全跳过这些计算，直接把假期过到 2017 年：超过一半的美国工人每年都没有用完所有分配的假期。

paragraphs.sourceText: Not so long ago, people would have turned up their noses at that kind of dedication to the job. As marketing professors Silvia Bellezza, Neeru Paharia, and Anat Keinan recently explained in Harvard Business Review (HBR), leisure time was once seen as an indicator of high social status, something attainable only for those at the top. Since the middle of the 20th century, though, things have turned the opposite way – these days, punishing hours at your desk, rather than days off, are seen as the mark of someone important.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不久前，人们还会对这种对工作的奉献精神嗤之以鼻。正如营销学教授 Silvia Bellezza、Neeru Paharia 和 Anat Keinan 最近在《哈佛商业评论》(HBR) 上所解释的那样，休闲时间曾经被视为高社会地位的指标，只有高层人士才能获得。然而，自 20 世纪中叶以来，情况发生了相反的变化——如今，在办公桌上度过痛苦的时间而不是休息日，被视为重要人物的标志。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a series of several experiments, the researchers illustrated just how much we’ve come to admire busyness, or at least the appearance of it. Volunteers read two passages, on about a man who led a life of leisure and another about a man who was over-worked and over –scheduled; when asked to determine which of the two had a higher social status, the majority of the participants said the latter. The same held true for people who used products that implied they were short on time: In one experiment, for example, customers of the grocery-delivery service Peapod were seen as of higher status than people who shopped at grocery stores that were equally expensive; in another, people wearing wireless headphones were considered further up on the social ladder than those wearing regular headphones, even when both were just used to listen to music.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在一系列的实验中，研究人员展示了我们是多么欣赏忙碌，或者至少是它的外表。志愿者们读了两篇文章，一篇是关于一个过着悠闲生活的人的，另一篇是关于一个过度工作和日程安排过多的人的；当被问及两者中谁的社会地位更高时，大多数参与者都说后者。对于那些使用暗示自己时间紧迫的产品的人来说也是如此：例如，在一项实验中，杂货配送服务 Peapod 的顾客被认为比在同样昂贵的杂货店购物的顾客地位更高；在另一项研究中，佩戴无线耳机的人被认为比佩戴普通耳机的人处于更高的社会地位，即使两者都只是用来听音乐。

paragraphs.sourceText: In part, the authors wrote in HBR, this pattern may have to do with the way work itself has changed over the past several decades.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作者在《哈佛商业评论》中写道，这种模式可能与过去几十年来工作方式本身的变化有关。

paragraphs.sourceText: We think that the shift from leisure-as-status to busyness-as-status may be linked to the development of knowledge-intensive economics. In such economies, individuals who possess the human capital characteristics that employers or clients value(e.g., competence and ambition) are expected to be in high demand and short supply on the job market. Thus, by telling others that we are busy and working all the time, we are implicitly suggesting that we are sought after, which enhances our perceived status.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们认为，从休闲状态到忙碌状态的转变可能与知识密集型经济的发展有关。在这样的经济体中，拥有雇主或客户看重的人力资本特征（例如能力和雄心）的个人预计在就业市场上会供不应求。因此，通过告诉别人我们很忙，一直在工作，我们就含蓄地暗示我们受到追捧，这提高了我们的感知地位。

paragraphs.sourceText: Even if you feel tempted to sacrifice your own vacation days for fake busyness, though, at least consider leaving your weekends unscheduled. It’s for your own good.
paragraphs.translationZh: 即使你很想为了假装忙碌而牺牲自己的假期，至少也要考虑一下不安排周末的时间。这是为了你好。
